Lessons.Title: Same Digit, Different Value
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will describe the value of a digit in one place as having ten times the value of the same digit in a place to its right.
This lesson shifts the focus from reading and writing numbers to describing the multiplicative relationship between place values in a multi-digit number. In previous lessons, you used base-ten blocks to represent large numbers, and wrote numbers in expanded form. In this lesson, you use your developing understanding of the value of a digit to begin to articulate that a digit in one place is ten times the value as the same digit in a place to its right.
Core relationship: Digit value depends on position. In a base-ten numeral, value of digit d in position p is d×10^p.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  True or False: Expanded Expressions	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Card Sort: Large Numbers	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Expand Large Numbers	 (15 minutes); Cool-down: The Value of Digits (5 minutes)

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Naming the digit instead of its place value.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: In a base-ten numeral, value of digit d in position p is d×10^p.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating 60,000 as the same value as 6,000.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The stated place value, scale, or arithmetic relationship is not preserved.
